findings.claim: The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear fits over the full observed window [0.0,0.5] with extrapolation disallowed and no accepted polynomial; the landmark soft-mass and local-derivative features show large first-vs-last rate z-scores with multiple sign changes, so a constant (time-invariant) contrast rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay within the observed support.

Several landmark local-derivative features carry strong sign conflicts (e.g. 9-14 conflicting batches) and high relative node RMSE, indicating the marginal coordinate descriptors are unstable across batches and should not be averaged into a single absolute geometric target.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control, and the learning window is [0.0,0.5] with recorded affinities removed and an equal score prior; therefore observed coordinate contrasts are selection/score-clock evidence, not absolute affinity benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: a constant rule matches or exceeds the observed-node fit fidelity (relative node RMSE) of the time-conditioned rule across the window
hypotheses.observable: observed-node contrast values of landmark soft-mass and local-derivative features across the observed score times
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule that follows the observed-node linear rate changes of landmark soft-mass and local-derivative features within [0.0,0.5] will track the observed contrast better than a constant rule, without extrapolation.

hypotheses.falsifier: a marginal descriptor with high sign conflicts still reproduces the observed contrast with low RMSE and consistent batch sign
hypotheses.statement: Marginal landmark local-derivative descriptors with many strong sign conflicts are not reliable standalone coordinate targets and should be treated as coupled/joint patterns rather than isolated marginals.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or final affinity outcomes are supplied; last-record/selection credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Descendant survival/quality credit, turnover accounting, joint covariance/mode diagnostics and multiplicity-adjusted ranking tables were not read in this turn, so A1.2, A2.1, A3.2 and A4.2 comparisons remain unsupported here.
Contrast curves are coordinate/score-clock contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies; no neural-module causation is claimed.
No temperature edit is proposed or permitted; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
